blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how profits are shared among partners in a business? Let's explore how partnership accounts work.

blocks.markdown: In a partnership, two or more individuals come together to run a business. The partnership agreement outlines how profits and losses are shared, but what happens if there is no agreement? This is where the Partnership Act provisions come into play.

blocks.title: Partnership Act Provisions
blocks.text: When there is no agreement, the Partnership Act states that profits and losses are shared equally, no interest on capital is allowed, and no partner is entitled to a salary.

blocks.markdown: Let's look at how to prepare an appropriation account. This account shows how the profit of a partnership is distributed among partners. It includes interest on capital, partners' salaries, and the share of profit.

blocks.title: Preparing an Appropriation Account
blocks.prompt: Consider a partnership with two partners, Aisha and Chinedu. The partnership agreement allows for interest on capital at 5%, salaries of ₦50,000 each, and the remaining profit shared equally. The profit for the year is ₦300,000. Prepare the appropriation account.

steps.text: Calculate interest on capital for both partners.
Subtract the total interest and salaries from the profit to find the residual profit.
Share the residual profit equally between the partners.

blocks.answer: Interest on Capital: ₦15,000 each; Salaries: ₦50,000 each; Residual Profit: ₦170,000; Share of Profit: ₦85,000 each.

blocks.markdown: Partners' current accounts track their transactions with the partnership, while capital accounts reflect their long-term investment. It's important to keep these accounts updated to reflect each partner's financial relationship with the business.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Always check if there's a partnership agreement before applying the provisions of the Partnership Act in questions.

points: Without an agreement, the Partnership Act dictates profit sharing and other terms.
An appropriation account helps distribute profits based on interest, salaries, and the remaining profit.
